paper.title: TORL-VLA: Tactile Guided Online Reinforcement Learning for Contact-Rich Manipulation

claim: Tactile-derived wrench (6D force/torque) supervision is essential beyond action labels for contact-rich manipulation, as it enables both future wrench prediction as a contact reference signal and online RL refinement conditioned on wrench feedback.

evidence.summary: TORL-VLA introduces a tactile-derived wrench-aware VLA that jointly predicts reference actions and future wrench sequences. The wrench token (6D force + 6D torque from two fingertip tactile sensors) is fused via MoE routing after visual-language encoding. The future wrench prediction objective (FWP) provides a contact reference signal. The online RL module conditions on measured wrench feedback for action refinement. Ablation shows removing MoE fusion causes the largest degradation (Cup: 30->18/30), and removing wrench history token or future wrench prediction each reduce success. The intervention-censored critic prevents post-intervention success from being wrongly credited to preceding policy actions.
evidence.locator: Section 3.1 (Tactile-Aware VLA as Reference), Section 3.2 (Online Reference Adaptation), Table 2 (Ablation)
evidence.short_quote: Our method introduces a tactile-derived wrench-aware VLA to predict reference actions and future wrench sequences, while a lightweight online RL module is used to refine the reference actions.

notes: Supervision type: tactile/force (wrench prediction + wrench-conditioned online RL)

paper_reading.relation: Evidence about non-action supervision signals for embodied models
paper_reading.verification_rationale: The paper directly demonstrates that wrench (force/torque) supervision beyond action labels improves contact-rich manipulation, with ablation evidence showing each wrench component contributes to performance.

paper.title: TORL-VLA: Tactile Guided Online Reinforcement Learning for Contact-Rich Manipulation

claim: An intervention-censored critic is needed to handle credit assignment bias when learning from mixed policy-generated and human-intervention data, preventing false credit propagation across correction boundaries.

evidence.summary: When human intervention occurs during online RL, a standard value function may wrongly credit preceding policy-generated actions for post-intervention success. The intervention-censored critic blocks post-intervention success from propagating back across human-correction boundaries. Diagnostics show the IC critic separates boundary chunks from clean chunks with AUC 0.999, while the task critic achieves only 0.565. The IC-hinge-active boundary contexts decrease from 53.94% at 10k steps to 12.73% at final checkpoint, showing the actor progressively avoids intervention-risky actions.
evidence.locator: Section 3.2 (Intervention-Censored Critic), Appendix A.4.2 (IC Critic Diagnostics), Table 7
evidence.short_quote: We introduce an intervention-censored critic that prevents post-intervention success from being wrongly credited to policy-generated actions preceding intervention.

notes: Supervision type: safety/corrective (intervention-censored value learning for credit assignment)

paper_reading.relation: Evidence about non-action supervision signals for embodied models
paper_reading.verification_rationale: This evidence shows that beyond action supervision, a specialized credit-assignment supervision signal is needed when human interventions are involved in contact-rich RL.

paper.title: PhysVLA: Towards Physically-Grounded VLA for Embodied Robotic Manipulation

claim: Physics supervision through a phase-aware finite-state machine and selective Euler-Lagrange dynamics gate is needed at inference time beyond action labels to enforce rigid-body dynamics and contact constraints that VLA models trained on demonstrations do not inherently respect.

evidence.summary: PhysVLA is a plug-and-play inference-time framework that wraps any frozen VLA backbone without retraining. It applies dual-layered correction: (i) a phase-aware FSM structuring discrete task segments (approach, grasp, transport, place) with phase-specific corrections, and (ii) a selective Euler-Lagrange gate that fires only when the dynamics residual exceeds a threshold (tau=0.1 N*m), using inertia-weighted correction. PhysVLA delivers up to 17% absolute success rate increase and 19% stability increase with zero per-task regressions. Temporal smoothing (uniform EMA) degrades success on every single-step backbone (OpenVLA: 36->28%), while PhysVLA improves it (36->53%). Real-world transfer on Agilex Piper shows 50% success improvement.
evidence.locator: Section 3.3 (PhysVLA Design), Section 3.2 (Empirical Results: Physics Gap), Table 3
evidence.short_quote: Because they are trained primarily to fit behavioural demonstration data, they do not explicitly enforce fundamental physical principles such as rigid-body dynamics or contact constraints.

notes: Supervision type: physics (Euler-Lagrange dynamics gate + phase-aware FSM at inference)

paper_reading.relation: Evidence about non-action supervision signals for embodied models
paper_reading.verification_rationale: The paper shows that physics-based supervision (dynamics constraints) is needed even at inference time, as VLA models trained on demonstrations alone produce physically inconsistent actions. The conditional activation (only when residual exceeds threshold) is a key design insight.

paper.title: CLAMP: Contrastive Learning for 3D Multi-View Action-Conditioned Robotic Manipulation Pretraining

claim: Contrastive learning that aligns 3D geometric representations (multi-view point cloud renderings), action patterns, and spatial-temporal text descriptions is needed beyond action label supervision for improving policy fine-tuning efficiency and performance.

evidence.summary: CLAMP contrastively pre-trains an image encoder, text encoder, and action encoder on large-scale simulated robot data. From merged point clouds, it re-renders multi-view four-channel observations (depth + 3D coordinates) including dynamic wrist views. The encoders learn to associate 3D geometric and positional information with robot action patterns via contrastive learning. STRING relative positional encoding enables tokens from different views corresponding to nearby 3D regions to be correlated. Pre-training both encoders and Diffusion Policy yields substantially better performance than pre-training encoders alone. Dynamic wrist views are critical for high-precision tasks. CLAMP outperforms SOTA across 6 simulated and 5 real-world tasks.

paper.title: Learning Geometrically-Grounded 3D Visual Representations for View-Generalizable Robotic Manipulation

claim: Multi-view geometric supervision through point cloud reconstruction and feed-forward Gaussian splatting, combined with distillation-based policy learning, is needed beyond action labels for view-generalizable robotic manipulation.

evidence.summary: GEM3D introduces a single-view 3D pretraining paradigm: (1) encoding RGB-D into volumetric features, (2) coarse-to-fine point cloud reconstruction supervised by multi-view ground-truth point clouds (Chamfer distance), and (3) feed-forward 3D Gaussian splatting supervised by multi-view RGB observations (focal loss). During policy learning, multi-step distillation aligns the policy encoder's latent features with pretrained representations via cosine-similarity distillation loss. GEM3D outperforms SOTA by 12.7% on 12 RLBench tasks. Zero-shot view generalization shows only 22.0% and 29.7% success drops under moderate/large viewpoint shifts vs SOTA's 41.6% and 51.5%. The distillation approach preserves geometric knowledge better than direct fine-tuning.

paper.title: Beyond Imitation: Reinforcement Learning-Based Sim-Real Co-Training for VLA Models

claim: SFT-based sim-real co-training is insufficient because it treats simulation as static demonstrations without exploiting large-scale closed-loop interaction, requiring RL reward supervision to achieve real-world generalization gains.

evidence.summary: The paper argues that most sim-real co-training methods rely on supervised fine-tuning (SFT), which treats simulation as a static source of demonstrations and does not exploit large-scale closed-loop interaction. Consequently, real-world gains and generalization are often limited. RL co-training yields stronger generalization to unseen task variations and substantially improved real-world data efficiency. The auxiliary supervised loss on real-world data is needed specifically to prevent catastrophic forgetting during RL fine-tuning in simulation, showing that RL supervision alone (without real-world anchoring) would degrade real-world performance.

paper.title: RoboInter1.5: A Holistic Intermediate Representation Suite for Embodied World Modeling and Robotic Manipulation

claim: Intermediate representations serve as structured conditioning signals for controllable world state prediction (RoboInter-World), demonstrating that semantic supervision (subtasks, contact points, affordance) is needed beyond action labels to constrain latent rollouts of physical simulators.

evidence.summary: RoboInter-World leverages intermediate representations as structured conditioning signals for controllable prediction of future world states. Rather than treating intermediate representations merely as interpretable signals, RoboInter1.5 conceptualizes them as a bidirectional interface that both regularizes low-level action spaces and constrains the latent rollouts of open-world physical simulators. The framework provides 10+ types of per-frame annotations including subtasks, primitive skills, object and gripper grounding, segmentation, affordance, grasp poses, contact points, and motion traces across 230k episodes and 571 scenes.

paper.title: OmniVTA: Visuo-Tactile World Modeling for Contact-Rich Robotic Manipulation

claim: Existing visuo-tactile methods treat tactile signals as passive observations rather than using them to model contact dynamics or enable closed-loop control, highlighting a gap in how tactile supervision is utilized beyond mere input conditioning.

evidence.summary: The paper identifies that current methods treat tactile signals as passive observations rather than using them to model contact dynamics or enable closed-loop control explicitly. OmniVTA addresses this by integrating a two-stream visuo-tactile world model for predicting short-horizon contact evolution and a 60Hz reflexive controller that corrects deviations between predicted and observed tactile signals. The OmniViTac dataset comprises 21,000+ trajectories across 86 tasks organized into six physics-grounded interaction patterns. This identifies a gap: most existing tactile-enhanced VLA methods use tactile data only as additional input, not as a supervision signal for contact dynamics modeling.
evidence.locator: Abstract, Introduction (identifying limitations of existing methods)
